messages.subject: Truncated Latent Normal Sampler
parts:
Hi, I have an ordered multivariate response, y[i,j], that i wish to model by introducing a latent response, t[i,j], on which i impose a set of (independent) normal priors  truncated by ordered cutpoints, c[j,k], where c[j,y[i,j] - 1] < t[i,j] <= c[j,y[i,j]] .  I choose this approach instead of employing the 'ordered_logistic' distribution because I will later generalize the implied normal link function by replacing the normal on t[i,j] with a mixture of normals.  

Stan does not yet allow me to declare constraints on each of the t[i,j] based on the y[i,j] in the parameters block.   So i would declare them as unrestricted.  Then in the models block i would impose a set of truncated normal distributions on the t[i,j] with the left and right truncation points for each t[i,j] based on the values of  c[j] and y[i,j].   Do I need to perform a series of Jacobian adjustments to lp_ to account for the transformation of the t[i,j] from restricted/truncated to unrestricted for HMC sampling since i didn't declare the t[i,j] as restricted in the parameters block?  In particular, I think page 164 of the manual shows the form of the transform and adjustment from restricted to unrestricted performed by Stan for 2-sided range restrictions? Alternatively, does the employment of the truncated normal distributions on the t[i,j] in the model block effectively communicate the range restrictions on the t[i,j] such that Stan would automatically perform the jacobian adjustment to unrestricted.

Lastly, am I required to manually input initial values for "t" and "c" in order to ensure the sampler finds coherence to observed "y" on launch?

Thanks, Terrance

--
Thank you, Terrance Savitsky
